dv.title: ޑޮމިނިކަން ރިޕަބްލިކްގެ ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރަށް އެ ގައުމުގެ މިނިވަން ދުވަހުގެ ތަހުނިޔާ ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގެ ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރު ފޮނުއްވައިފި
dv.description: ‏‎ ޑޮމިނިކަން ރިޕަބްލިކްގެ މިނިވަން ދުވަހުގެ މުނާސަބަތުގައި އެޤައުމުގެ ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރު، ރޮބާޓޯ އަލްވަރޭޒް ގިލް އަށް ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގެ ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރު، ޑޮކްޓަރ ޢަބްދުﷲ ޚަލީލް ތަހުނިޔާގެ މެސެޖެއް ފޮނުއްވައިފިއެވެ.
dv.body:
Ref: 2025/PR/60

‏‎ ޑޮމިނިކަން ރިޕަބްލިކްގެ މިނިވަން ދުވަހުގެ މުނާސަބަތުގައި އެޤައުމުގެ ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރު، ރޮބާޓޯ އަލްވަރޭޒް ގިލް އަށް ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގެ ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރު، ޑޮކްޓަރ ޢަބްދުﷲ ޚަލީލް ތަހުނިޔާގެ މެސެޖެއް ފޮނުއްވައިފިއެވެ.

‏‎މިނިސްޓަރުގެ މެސެޖު ތިރީގައި މިވަނީއެވެ.

"ދިވެހި ސަރުކާރާއި ދިވެހި ރައްޔިތުންގެ ނަމުގައި، އަދި އަޅުގަނޑުގެ އަމިއްލަ ނަމުގައި މަނިކުފާނަށާއި ޑޮމިނިކަން ރިޕަބްލިކް ސަރުކާރަށާއި ރައްޔިތުންނަށް، ޑޮމިނިކަން ރިޕަބްލިކްގެ މިނިވަން ދުވަހުގެ ތަހުނިޔާ އާއި ހެޔޮއެދުންތައް އަރިސްކުރަމެވެ.

ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއާއި ޑޮމިނިކަން ރިޕަބްލިކް އަކީ ތަރައްޤީވަމުން އަންނަ ކުދި ޖަޒީރާ ޤައުމުތަކުގެ ތެރޭގައި ހިމެނޭ ދެ ޤައުމު ކަމުގައިވާތީ، ކުރިޔަށް އޮތް އަހަރުތަކުގައިވެސް، ޑޮމިނިކަން ރިޕަބްލިކް އާއި ރާއްޖެއާ ދެމެދު އޮންނަ ގުޅުން އިތުރަށް ބަދަހިވެގެންދާނެކަމުގައި އަޅުގަނޑު ޔަޤީންކުރަމެވެ.

‏‎އަޅުގަނޑު މަނިކުފާނަށް ކުރާ މަތިވެރި ޤަދަރު އާކޮށް، އެކަން ޔަޤީންކޮށް އެރުވުމަށް މި ފުރުސަތުގެ ބޭނުންކުރީމެވެ."

ނިމުނީ

en.title: Minister of Foreign Affairs concludes his visit to Geneva after participating in the High-level segment of the 58th session of the Human Rights Council
en.description: Minister of Foreign Affairs, Dr. Abdulla Khaleel, departed from Geneva, Switzerland today after participating in the High-level Segment of the 58th Session of the Human Rights Council from 24-25 February 2025.
en.body:
Ref: 2025/PR/59

Minister of Foreign Affairs, Dr. Abdulla Khaleel, departed from Geneva, Switzerland today after participating in the High-level Segment of the 58th Session of the Human Rights Council from 24-25 February 2025.  
  
During his visit, Minister Dr. Khaleel delivered the Maldives’ national statement at the High-level General Debate of the 58th Session of the Human Rights Council. In his statement, he reaffirmed the Maldives’ commitment to fulfilling Maldives’ international obligations and advancing the pursuit to promote and protect human rights.  
  
In addition, he met with High Commissioner for Human Rights, Mr. Volker Türk and President of the Human Rights Council, Mr. Jürg Lauber, along with heads of delegations of Palestine, Qatar, Costa Rica, Bahrain, Serbia, Iceland and Azerbaijan on the sidelines of the session. He also met with the Director General of WIPO.  
  
Minister Dr. Khaleel participated as a panellist in three side events in the margins of the session. These events include a panel discussion organised by the Permanent Mission of the Maldives on advancing the right to a clean, healthy and sustainable environment, a discussion organised by the Permanent Mission of Estonia on Internet shutdowns and the role of the Freedom Online Coalition, and a side event organised by the Permanent Mission of Slovenia on Advancing Equality through Multilateralism.  
  
The Maldives is currently a Member of the Human Rights Council. This is the third time the Maldives is serving on the Human Rights Council and during its time as a Member, the Maldives has been active in making significant contributions to the Council’s work.

ENDS

en.title: Maldives National University together with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs hosts model Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting
en.description: The Maldives National University (MNU) in collaboration with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs held a model Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM) today.
en.body:
Ref: 2025/PR/58

The Maldives National University (MNU) in collaboration with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs held a model Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM) today.

In the lead up to Commonwealth Day on 10 March 2025, the model CHOGM was held under this year’s theme for the Commonwealth Day “Together we thrive”. The event simulated the Executive Sessions of CHOGM, bringing together students from various batches of the Faculty of Arts of MNU. It provided them with the platform to engage in a productive discussion, raising critical issues and challenges vital to the Commonwealth, including climate change, sustainable development, and economic resilience.

During the session, the students reflected on the shared values of the Commonwealth, emphasising the importance of fostering cooperation and youth involvement across the Commonwealth in addressing global challenges. The model CHOGM session served as part of the broader Commonwealth Day commemorations, reinforcing the Maldives’ commitment to empowering young people in shaping the future of the Commonwealth.

The event was attended by the senior officials of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, senior officials of the Maldives National University, representatives from the diplomatic community, as well as university and high school students.  
  
ENDS

dv.title: ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގެ ޤައުމީ ޔުނިވަރސިޓީ އާއި މިނިސްޓްރީ އޮފް ފޮރިން އެފެއާޒްއާ ގުޅިގެން މޮޑެލް ކޮމަންވެލްތު އިސްވެރިގެން ބައްދަލުވުމެއް ބާއްވާއިފި
dv.description: ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގެ ޤައުމީ ޔުނިވަރސިޓީ އާއި މިނިސްޓްރީ އޮފް ފޮރިން އެފެއާޒް އާ ގުޅިގެން ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގައި މޮޑެލް ކޮމަންވެލްތު އިސްވެރިގެން ބައްދަލުވުމެއް ބާއްވައިފިއެވެ.
dv.body:
Ref: 2025/PR/58

ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގެ ޤައުމީ ޔުނިވަރސިޓީ އާއި މިނިސްޓްރީ އޮފް ފޮރިން އެފެއާޒް އާ ގުޅިގެން ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގައި މޮޑެލް ކޮމަންވެލްތު އިސްވެރިގެން ބައްދަލުވުމެއް ބާއްވައިފިއެވެ.

މިއަންނަ މާރޗް މަހުގެ 10 ވަނަ ދުވަހު ފާހަގަކުރާ ކޮމަންވެލްތު ދުވަހާ ގުޅުވައިގެން ބޭއްވި މި މޮޑެލް ކޮމަންވެލްތު އިސްވެރިންގެ ބައްދަލުވުމުގެ ޝިޢާރަކީ މި އަހަރުގެ ކޮމަންވެލްތު ދުވަހުގެ ޝިޢާރުކަމުގައިވާ "ޓުގެދަރ ވީ ތްރައިވް" އެވެ. މި ސެޝަންގައި ދައްކުވައިދީފައިވަނީ ކޮމަންވެލްތު އިސްވެރިންގެ ބައްދަލުވުމުގެ އެގްޒެކެޓިވް ސެޝަންއެއް ހިނގާ ގޮތެވެ. ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގެ ޤައުމީ ޔުނިވަރސިޓީގެ ފެކަލްޓީ އޮފް އާރޓްސްގެ އެކި ބެޗުތަކުގެ ދަރިވަރުން މި މޮޑެލް ސެޝަންގައި ބައިވެރިވެރިވެ، ކޮމަންވެލްތު ގައުމުތަކަށް ދިމާވާ ގޮންޖެހުންތަކާ ގުޅޭގޮތުން، ޚާއްސަކޮށް، މޫސުމަށް އަންނަ ބަދަލުތަކުގެ ސަބަބުން ކުރާ ނޭދެވޭ އަސަރާއި، ދެމެހެއްޓެނިވި ތަރައްޤީ އަދި އިޤްތިސާދީ ވިލުންތެރިކަން އިތުރުކުރުމާ ގުޅޭގޮތުން މަޝްވަރާކުރިއެވެ. މި މަޝްވަރާތަކުގައި ދަރިވަރުން ވަނީ ކޮމަންވެލްތުގެ ހަމަތަކަށް އަލިއަޅުވާލައި އެއްބާރުލުން އިތުރުކޮށް ދުނިޔެއަށް ދިމާވާ އެކި ގޮންޖެހުންތަކާ ކުރިމަތިލުމަށް ކަނޑައަޅާ ސިޔާސަތުތައް އެކުލަވާލާއިރު ޒުވާނުންގެ ބައިވެރިވުން މުހިންމުކަން ފާހަކޮށްފައެވެ. މި މޮޑެލް ސެޝަންއިން ކޮމަންވެލްތުގެ މުސްތަޤްބަލް ބައްޓަންކުރުމަށްޓަކައި ޒުވާނުންގެ ބައިވެރިވުން އިތުރުކުރުމަށް ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއިން އަހައްމިއްޔަތުކަން ދޭ މިންވަރު ހާމަވެގެންދިޔައެވެ.

މި މޮޑެލް ކޮމަންވެލްތު އިސްވެރިގެން ބައްދަލުވުމުގައި މިނިސްޓްރީ އޮފް ފޮރިން އެފެއާޒް އަދި ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގެ ޤައުމީ ޔުނިވަރސިޓީގެ އިސްވެރިން، ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގައި ގާއިމްކޮށްފައިވާ އެކި ގައުމުތަކުގެ ހައި ކޮމިޝަން އަދި އެމްބަސީ ގެ އިސްބޭފުޅުން، އަދި ޔުނިވަރސިޓީ އަދި ހައި ސްކޫލް ދަރިވަރުން ބައިވެރިވިއެވެ.

en.title: Maldives Calls for Greater Gender Equality in Global Diplomacy at the Human Rights Council
en.description: The Maldives co-hosted a High-Level side event alongside Slovenia, Morocco, Spain, Thailand, UN Women and the Universal Rights Group entitled “Implementing Foreign Policy Goals with a Human Rights Lens: Advancing…
en.body:
Ref: 2025/PR/57

The Maldives co-hosted a High-Level side event alongside Slovenia, Morocco, Spain, Thailand, UN Women and the Universal Rights Group entitled “Implementing Foreign Policy Goals with a Human Rights Lens: Advancing Equality through Multilateralism” on the margins of the 58th Session of the Human Rights Council.

The event brought together high-level officials and experts for a panel discussion on the role of women in multilateralism. The dialogue focused on strengthening women's participation and leadership in addressing pressing global challenges, including threats to peace, sustainable development, and human rights.

Minister of Foreign Affairs Dr. Abdulla Khaleel was among the panelists of the event. In his remarks, Minister Khaleel underscored the commitment of the Maldives to fostering a more inclusive diplomatic landscape. He particularly highlighted the achievements of the Maldivian Foreign Service in promoting gender parity, including the historic appointment of the first female Foreign Secretary.

Speaking further Minister Khaleel stated that “The Maldives has always believed in a multilateral system that is inclusive, representative, and responsive to the needs of all.”  
He then reflected on the key role played by the Maldives in leading the United Nations General Assembly resolution establishing June 24th as the International Day of Women in Diplomacy.

Before concluding, Minister Khaleel emphasised the need to strengthen institutional frameworks to eliminate gender bias in recruitment and leadership. He highlighted the importance of building robust mentorship and leadership programs to empower women in diplomacy. He also called on multilateral organisations to lead by example, urging the appointment of the first-ever female UN Secretary-General as a significant step toward greater gender equality in global governance.

The Maldives remains committed to gender equality and inclusive diplomacy, on the recognition that true multilateral progress depends on ensuring all voices are heard and all individuals have equal opportunities to lead.

ENDS

en.title: Minister Dr. Abdulla Khaleel reaffirmed Maldives’ commitment to ‘keep the internet on’ at the Freedom Online Coalition event on the sidelines of the High-Level Segment of the 58th Session of the Human Rights Council
en.description: The Minister of Foreign Affairs Dr. Abdulla Khaleel today spoke at the ‘Keep the Internet On! The Impact of Internet Shutdowns’ event hosted by the Permanent Mission of Estonia on behalf of Freedom Online Coalition on…
en.body:
Ref: 2025/PR/56

The Minister of Foreign Affairs Dr. Abdulla Khaleel today spoke at the ‘Keep the Internet On! The Impact of Internet Shutdowns’ event hosted by the Permanent Mission of Estonia on behalf of Freedom Online Coalition on the sidelines of the High-Level Segment of the 58th Session of the Human Rights Council, taking place in Geneva, Switzerland.

Minister Dr. Khaleel noted the remarkable progress which the Maldives has made in expanding digital access and highlighted on the outcomes of the national efforts to bridge the digital divide. Further, Minister Dr. Khaleel emphasized the importance of digital connectivity for Small Island Developing States such as the Maldives in terms of education, healthcare and industry.

Expressing that the geographically dispersed nature of the Maldives poses a natural challenge to connectivity, Minister Dr. Khaleel called for solutions based on collective action to ensure that the internet remains open, secure and accessible to all.

In conclusion, Minister Dr. Khaleel reaffirmed the Maldives commitment to working with its bilateral and multilateral partners to ensure that the benefits of digitalization are shared equitably, to bridge the digital divide and to ‘keep the internet on’ as a space of opportunity, possibility and creativity.

ENDS

en.title: Minister Dr. Khaleel sends National Day and Liberation Day greetings to the Foreign Minister of Kuwait
en.description: The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives Dr. Abdulla Khaleel sends message of felicitations to the Minister of Foreign Affairs of the State of Kuwait, Abdulla Ali Al-Yahya, on the occasion of the…
en.body:
Ref: 2025/PR/54

The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives Dr. Abdulla Khaleel sends message of felicitations to the Minister of Foreign Affairs of the State of Kuwait, Abdulla Ali Al-Yahya, on the occasion of the National Day and the Liberation Day of the State of Kuwait.

Minister's message reads as follows:

"Excellency,

Let me extend warm felicitations and well wishes to Your Excellency, the Government and the brotherly people of the State of Kuwait, on the auspicious occasions of Kuwait’s National Day on the 25 February and Liberation Day on 26 February.

The Maldives and Kuwait shares an enduring friendship deeply rooted in our common Islamic values, culture, and history, a bond that has grown steadily stronger over the years.

I remain confident that the excellent relations, mutual respect, and cooperation between our two nations will continue to flourish in the years ahead.

May I also take this opportunity to convey my personal well wishes and prayers for Your Excellency’s good health and happiness, and for the lasting progress and prosperity and well-being for the people of Kuwait.

Please accept, Excellency, the assurances of my highest consideration."

ENDS

dv.title: ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރު ޑރ. ޚަލީލް ކުވައިތުގެ ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރަށް ޤައުމީ ދުވަސް އަދި ލިބަރޭޝަން ދުވަހުގެ ތަހުނިޔާ ފޮނުއްވައިފި
dv.description: ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރުގެ މެސެޖު ތިރީގައި އެވަނީއެވެ.
dv.body:
Ref: 2025/PR/54

ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރުގެ މެސެޖު ތިރީގައި އެވަނީއެވެ.

"ކުވައިތުގެ ޤައުމީ ދުވަސް އަދި ލިބަރޭޝަން ދުވަހުގެ މުނާސަބަތުގައި، ދިވެހި ސަރުކާރާއި ރައްޔިތުން އަދި އަޅުގަނޑުގެ އަމިއްލަ ނަމުގައި މަނިކުފާނަށާއި ކުވައިތުގެ ސަރުކާރަށް އަދި ރައްޔިތުންނަށް ވަރަށް އިޚްލާޞްތެރިކަމާއެކު ތަހުނިޔާއާއި ހެޔޮއެދުންތައް އަރިސްކުރަމެވެ.

ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއާއި ކުވައިތުގެ ގުޅުމަކީ އިސްލާމީ ރިވެތި އަޚްލާޤާއި ޘަޤާފަތާއި ތާރީޚުގެ ތެރޭގައި ގުޅިފައިވާ ދެމެހެއްޓެނިވި އެކުވެރި ގުޅުމެކެވެ.

ދެޤައުމުގެ ދެމެދުގައި އޮތް ގާތް ގުޅުން އަދި އެއްބާރުލުން ކުރިއަށް އޮތް އަހަރުތަކުގައި އިތުރަށް ބަދަހިވެގެންދާނެކަމަށް އަޅުގަނޑު ޔަޤީންކުރަމެވެ.

މި ފުރުސަތުގައި، މަނިކުފާނަށް ދުޅަހެޔޮ ޞިއްޙަތާއި ކުވައިތުގެ ރައްޔިތުންނަށް އުފާފާގަތި މުސްތަޤުބަލަކަށް އެދެމެވެ.

އަޅުގަނޑު މަނިކުފާނަށް ކުރާ މަތިވެރި ޤަދަރު އާކޮށް، އެކަން ޔަޤީންކޮށް އެރުވުމަށް މި ފުރުޞަތުގެ ބޭނުންކުރީމެވެ."

ނިމުނީ.

en.title: Maldives reaffirms its strong commitment to the promotion and protection of human rights at the 58th Session of the Human Rights Council
en.description: The Minister of Foreign Affairs, Dr. Abdulla Khaleel, today delivered the national statement at the High-level Segment of the 58th Session of the Human Rights Council, taking place in Geneva, Switzerland.
en.body:
Ref: 2025/PR/53

The Minister of Foreign Affairs, Dr. Abdulla Khaleel, today delivered the national statement at the High-level Segment of the 58th Session of the Human Rights Council, taking place in Geneva, Switzerland.

Reaffirming the commitment to fulfilling Maldives’ international obligations and advancing the pursuit to promote and protect human rights, Minister Dr. Khaleel reflected on Maldives’ achievements as a Member of the Human Rights Council, particularly the establishment of a voluntary trust fund for LDCs and SIDS and the international recognition of the right to a clean, healthy and sustainable environment. He cited these achievements as a testament to Maldives’ commitment to enhancing inclusivity in the Council’s work.

Further, Minister Dr. Khaleel emphasised that the promotion and protection of human rights is a key priority of President Dr. Muizzu’s administration, as evidenced by commitments and actions across a diverse range of sectors. In particular, Minister Dr. Khaleel highlighted the importance placed by the Government on addressing pertinent social issues such as gender equality and women’s empowerment, disability inclusiveness, providing adequate housing, and addressing vulnerability to the adverse impacts of climate change.

On the situation of Palestine, Minister Dr. Khaleel expressed deep concern for the destruction and loss of lives caused by Israel’s aggression against the people of Palestine. He emphasised Maldives’ longstanding relationship and solidarity with the people of Palestine.

The 58th Session of the Human Rights Council Session is being held from 24 February to 4 April 2025 in Geneva, Switzerland. The Maldives is a member of the Human Rights Council for the 2023 – 2025 term and actively engages in the Council.

dv.title: އިންސާނީ ޙައްޤުތައް ކުރިއަރުވައި ހިމާޔަތްކުރުމަށް ކުރަމުންދާ މަސައްކަތުގައި ސާބިތުކަމާއެކު ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއިން ކުރިއަށްދާނެކަމުގެ ޔަޤީންކަން މިނިސްޓަރ ޑރ. ޚަލީލް ދެއްވައިފި
dv.description: ސްވިޓްޒަލެންޑްގެ ޖެނީވާގައި މިހާރު ކުރިއަށްދާ އިންސާނީ ޙައްޤުތަކާ ބެހޭ މަޖިލީހުގެ 58 ވަނަ ސެޝަންގެ ހައިލެވެލް ސެގްމަންޓްގައި މިނިސްޓަރ އޮފް ފޮރިން އެފެއާޒް ޑރ. އަބްދުﷲ ޚަލީލް މިއަދު ތަޤުރީރުކުރައްވައިފިއެވެ.
dv.body:
Ref: 2025/PR/53

ސްވިޓްޒަލެންޑްގެ ޖެނީވާގައި މިހާރު ކުރިއަށްދާ އިންސާނީ ޙައްޤުތަކާ ބެހޭ މަޖިލީހުގެ 58 ވަނަ ސެޝަންގެ ހައިލެވެލް ސެގްމަންޓްގައި މިނިސްޓަރ އޮފް ފޮރިން އެފެއާޒް ޑރ. އަބްދުﷲ ޚަލީލް މިއަދު ތަޤުރީރުކުރައްވައިފިއެވެ.

ރާއްޖެއިން އެއްބަސްވެފައިވާ ބައިނަލްއަޤްވާމީ އިންސާނީ ޙައްޤުތަކާ ބެހޭ މުޢާހަދާތަކާއި އެންމެހައި ރައްޔިތުންގެ އިންސާނީ ޙައްޤުތައް ހިމާޔަތްކުރުމުގައި މި ސަރުކާރުން މަސައްކަތްކުރާނެކަމުގެ ޔަޤީންކަން އެމަނިކުފާނުގެ ތަޤްރީރުގައި ދެއްވިއެވެ. އަދި އިންސާނީ ޙައްޤުތަކާބެހޭ މަޖިލީހުގެ މެންބަރު ޤައުމެއްގެ ހައިސިއްޔަތުން ރާއްޖެއިން ކޮށްފައިވާ މަސައްކަތްތަކަށް ވަނީ އަލިއަޅުއްވާލައްވާފައެވެ. އެގޮތުން، އެންމެ ކުޑަކޮށް ތަރައްޤީވެފައިވާ ޤައުމުތަކާއި ތަރައްޤީވަމުން އަންނަ ކުދި ޖަޒީރާ ޤައުމުތައް ކައުންސިލްގެ މަސައްކަތުގައި ބައިވެރިވުމަށް މަގުފަހިކުރުމަށްޓަކައި ވޮލަންޓްރީ ޓްރަސްޓް ފަންޑެއް ޤާއިމުކުރުމާއި ސާފުތާހިރު، ދުޅަހެޔޮ، ދެމެހެއްޓެނިވި ތިމާވެށްޓަކީ އިންސާނީ ޙައްޤެއްކަން ދުނިޔޭގެ ފެންވަރުގައި ބަލައިގަތުމަށް ރާއްޖެއިން އަދާކޮށްފައިވާ އިސްދައުރު އެމަނިކުފާނު ފާހަގަކުރެއްވިއެވެ.

އެމަނިކުފާނުގެ ތަޤުރީރުގައި އިންސާނީ ޙައްޤުތައް ކުރިއެރުވުމަށާއި ޙިމާޔަތްކުރުމަށް ރައީސުލްޖުމްހޫރިއްޔާ ޑޮކްޓަރ މުޙައްމަދު މުޢިއްޒުގެ ސަރުކާރުން ކުރަމުންގެންދާ މަސައްކަތްތަކުގެ މައްޗަށް އަލިއަޅުއްވާލެއްވިއެވެ. އަދި، މިންތީގެ ހަމަހަމަކަމާއި އެކަށީގެންވާ ބޯހިޔާވަހިކަމާއި ނުކުޅެދުންތެރިކަން ހުންނަ ފަރާތްތައް މުޖުތަމައުގައި ބައިވެރިކުރުން އިތުރުކުރުމާއި މޫސުމަށް އަންނަ ބަދަލުތަކުގެ ސަބަބުން ތިމާވެއްޓާއި އެވެށީގައި ދިރިއުޅޭ ފަރާތްތަކަށް ކުރާ ނޭދެވޭ އަސަރުތައް ކުޑަކުރުން ފަދަ އިޖުތިމާއީ ކަންކަމަށް ސަރުކާރުން ދޭ އަހަންމިއްޔަތުގެ މައްޗަށް ވެސް އެމަނިކުފާނު ވާހަކަފުޅު ދެއްކެވިއެވެ.  
  
މީގެ އިތުރުން، ފަލަޞްޠީނުގެ ރައްޔިތުންނަށް އިސްރާއީލުން ދީފައިވާ ލާއިންސާނީ ޙަމަލާތަކުގެ ސަބަބުން ލިބިފައިވާ ގެއްލުންތަކާއި ގެއްލިފައިވާ ފުރާނަތަކުގެ މައްޗަށް މިނިސްޓަރ ޑރ. ޚަލީލްގެ ވާހަކަފުޅުގައި ކަންބޮޑުވުން ފާޅުކުރެއްވިއެވެ. އަދި ފަލަޞްޠީނާއި ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއާ ދެމެދު އޮތް ޒަމާންވީ ގުޅުމުގެ މައްޗަށް އަލިއަޅުއްވާލެއްވިއެވެ.

އިންސާނީ ޙައްޤުތަކާ ބެހޭ މަޖިލީހުގެ 58 ވަނަ ސެޝަން ކުރިއަށް ދަނީ 24 ފެބްރުއަރީ އިން 4 އޭޕްރީލް 2025 އަށް ސްވިޓްޒަލޭންޑްގެ ޖެނީވާގައެވެ. ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއަކީ 2023 އިން 2025 ވަނަ އަހަރުގެ ނިޔަލަށް އ.ދ. ގެ އިންސާނީ ޙައްޤުތަކާ ބެހޭ މަޖިލީހުގެ މެމްބަރު ޤައުމެކެވެ.

en.title: Maldives to participate in the 58th Session of the United Nations Human Rights Council
en.description: The 58th Session of the UN Human Rights Council commenced today in Geneva, Switzerland. The session opened with the High-Level Segment to be held from 24th February 2025 to 26th February 2025 followed by the General…
en.body:
Ref: 2025/PR/52

The 58th Session of the UN Human Rights Council commenced today in Geneva, Switzerland. The session opened with the High-Level Segment to be held from 24th February 2025 to 26th February 2025 followed by the General Segment, which will continue from 27th February 2025 to 4th April 2025.

His Excellency Dr. Abdulla Khaleel, Minister of Foreign Affairs will address the Human Rights Council today. In his statement, Minister Khaleel will brief the council on the progress made by the Government of Maldives, under the leadership of President Dr. Mohamed Muizzu in the promotion and protection of human rights. In his address, Minister Khaleel will also highlight the engagements of the government with the Office of the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights and the Special Procedures Mandate-holders. Moreover, Minister Khaleel will reaffirm the Maldives’ unwavering commitment to human rights and justice and advocate for equality and inclusion, particularly for Least Developed Countries and Small Island Developing States in the work of the Council.

As part of his engagements, Minister Khaleel will deliver a keynote address at a high-level side event organised by the Permanent Mission of Maldives together with the Core Group on the Right to a Healthy Environment. The event, titled ‘Advancing the Universal Human Right to a Clean, Healthy, and Sustainable Environment: Taking Stock and What Next?’, will be held on 24th February 2025. Additionally, he will participate in two panel discussions organised by the Permanent Mission of Slovenia and the Permanent Mission of Estonia on the sidelines of the High-Level Segment.

In line with the Government’s key policies and priorities, the Maldives delegation will deliver national statements under several agenda items during the General Segment. Furthermore, the Maldives, in partnership with the Core Group on the Right to a Healthy Environment, will present a resolution on the human right to a clean, healthy, and sustainable environment, with a particular focus on oceans and human rights. Additionally, Maldives alongside the Core Group on women in diplomacy will introduce a resolution on “Women, diplomacy and Human Rights” during this session.

The Maldives delegation for the High-Level Segment of the 58th Session of the Human Rights Council will be led by the Minister of Foreign Affairs, H.E. Dr. Abdulla Khaleel. The delegation will also include Her Excellency Dr. Salma Rasheed, Permanent Representative of the Maldives to the United Nations Offices at Geneva, Ms. Mariyam Midhfa Naeem, Joint Secretary of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Mr. Adam Hamid, Counsellor of the Maldives Mission to the United Nations Offices at Geneva, Ms. Aminath Shifaya Ibrahim, Counsellor of the Maldives Mission to the United Nations Offices at Geneva, Ms. Aishath Rayahyn, Second Secretary of the Maldives Mission to the United Nations Offices at Geneva, Mr. Amr Danyal Shamun, Chief General Service Officer of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Ms. Fathin Shoora Haleem, Third Secretary of the Maldives Mission to the United Nations Offices at Geneva, and Mr. Mohamed Raaidh Saeedh, Attaché of the Maldives Mission to the United Nations Offices at Geneva.  
ENDS

en.title: Maldives hosts a side event on Advancing the Right to Clean, Healthy and Sustainable Environment on the sidelines of the 58h session of the UN Human Rights Council
en.description: The Permanent Mission of Maldives, in collaboration with Costa Rica, Morocco, Slovenia, Switzerland and co-hosted by Office of the High Commissioner of Human Rights (OHCHR) hosted a Side Event titled “Advancing the…
en.body:
Ref: 2025/PR/55

The Permanent Mission of Maldives, in collaboration with Costa Rica, Morocco, Slovenia, Switzerland and co-hosted by Office of the High Commissioner of Human Rights (OHCHR) hosted a Side Event titled “*Advancing the universal human right to a clean, healthy, and sustainable environment: taking stock and what next?”* during the High-Level Segment of the 58th Session of the Human Right Council, today.

Ambassador Dr. Salma Rasheed, the Permanent Representative of Maldives to the United Nations, delivered the opening remarks, stressing the importance of moving from commitment to tangible actions in realizing the right to a clean, healthy and sustainable environment.

The key note address was presented by, Minister of Foreign Affairs Dr. Abdullah Khaleel. He reflected on the Maldives' long-standing leadership in climate advocacy, recalling the 1989 Malé Declaration on Sea Level Rise. Minister Khaleel also emphasised that for Small Island Developing States like the Maldives, the right to a clean environment is not just a policy issue but a matter of survival and security. In this regard, he called for continued global action to address the climate crisis and ensure the right to a clean, healthy and sustainable environment is fully and effectively implemented. Minister Khaleel then reaffirmed the Maldives' commitment to lead in shaping solutions for a sustainable future.

Following the keynote, a panel discussion featured H.E. Mr. Alejandro Solano Ortiz, Vice-Minister of Multilateral Affairs of Costa Rica, video message by Ms. Astrid Puentes Riaño, Special Rapporteur on the human right to a clean, healthy and sustainable environment, along with two representatives from the Civil Society. The discussion was moderated by Mr. Marc Limon, Executive Director, Universal Rights Group.

The purpose of the event was to assess the progress made since the UN Human Rights Council and the UN General Assembly adopted historic resolutions in 2021 and 2022, respectively, recognizing the right to a clean, healthy, and sustainable environment as a universal human right. The panelists discussed the steps taken by governments, international organizations, and civil society to implement and realize this right at the national, regional, and international levels.

Ambassador Anita Pipan, the Permanent Representative of Slovenia to the United Nations, delivered the closing remarks, emphasizing the need for the Human Rights Council and the wider UN human rights system to maintain their leadership and ambition in promoting the further advancement of this fundamental right.

The side event provided a valuable platform for stakeholders to take stock of the progress made and to identify the remaining challenges and opportunities in ensuring that everyone, everywhere, can enjoy the right to live in a clean, healthy, and sustainable environment.  
  
ENDS

en.title: Foreign Minister Dr. Khaleel sends Independence Day greetings to the Foreign Minister of Estonia
en.description: The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives, Dr. Abdulla Khaleel sends a message of felicitations to the Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Estonia, Margus Tsahkna, on the occasion of the…
en.body:
Ref: 2025/PR/51

The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives, Dr. Abdulla Khaleel sends a message of felicitations to the Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Estonia, Margus Tsahkna, on the occasion of the Independence Day of Estonia.

Minister's message reads as follow;

"On behalf of the Government and the people of the Maldives, I would like to extend warm greetings and sincere best wishes to Your Excellency, and the people of Estonia, on the auspicious occasion of your Independence Day.

It was both an honour and a privilege to accompany His Excellency  
Dr. Mohamed Muizzu, President of the Republic of Maldives, on his official visit to Estonia, this January.

I am confident that we can continue to work together to deepen the ties of friendship and cooperation between our two countries in the years ahead.

Let me also extend my best wishes for your good health, well-being, and continued prosperity for the people of Estonia.

Please accept, Excellency, the assurances of my highest consideration.

ENDS.

dv.title: ‎އެސްޓޯނިއާގެ ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރަށް އެ ޤައުމުގެ މިނިވަން ދުވަހުގެ ތަހުނިޔާ ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގެ ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރު ފޮނުއްވައިފި
dv.description: ‎އެސްޓޯނިއާގެ މިނިވަން ދުވަހުގެ މުނާސަބަތުގައި އެޤައުމުގެ ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރު، މާރްގުސް ސަޚްނާ އަށް ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގެ ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރު، ޑޮކްޓަރ ޢަބްދުﷲ ޚަލީލް ތަހުނިޔާގެ މެސެޖެއް ފޮނުއްވައިފި އެވެ.
dv.body:
Ref: 2025/PR/51

‎އެސްޓޯނިއާގެ މިނިވަން ދުވަހުގެ މުނާސަބަތުގައި އެޤައުމުގެ ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރު، މާރްގުސް ސަޚްނާ އަށް ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގެ ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރު، ޑޮކްޓަރ ޢަބްދުﷲ ޚަލީލް ތަހުނިޔާގެ މެސެޖެއް ފޮނުއްވައިފި އެވެ.

‎މިނިސްޓަރުގެ މެސެޖު ތިރީގައި މިވަނީއެވެ.

"ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގެ ސަރުކާރާއި ދިވެހި ރައްޔިތުންގެ ނަމުގައި އެސްޓޯނިއާގެ މިނިސްވަން ދުވަހުގެ މުނާސަބަތުގައި މަނިކުފާނަށާއި އެސްޓޯނިއާގެ ރައްޔިތުންނަށް އިޚްލާސްތެރި ތަހުނިޔާ އާއި ހެޔޮ އެދުންތައް އަރިސްކުރުމެވެ.

މިދިޔަ ޖަނަވަރީ މަހުގެ ތެރޭގައި ރައީސުލްޖުމްހޫރިއްޔާ ޑޮކްޓަރ މުޙައްމަދު މުޢިއްޒު، އެސްޓޯނިއާ އަށް ކުރެއްވި ރަސްމީ ދަތުރުފުޅުގައި އެމަނިކުފާނުގެ އަރިހުގައި އެސްޓޯނިއާ އަށް ދަތުރުކުރުމުގެ ފުރުސަތަކީ އަޅުގަނޑަށް ލިބުނު ޝަރަފެކެވެ.

ރައީސުލްޖުމްހޫރިއްޔާގެ ދަތުރުފުޅުގެ ތެރޭގައި ކުރެވުނު މަޝްވަރާތަކާއި ކުރިއަށް އޮތް ތާނގައި މަސައްކަތްކުރުމަށް ނިންމެވި ކަންތަކުގެ މައްޗަށް ބިނާކޮށް، ކުރިއަށް އޮތް ތާނގައިވެސް ދެޤައުމުގެ ދެމެދުގައި އޮތް އެކުވެރިކަމާއި އެއްބާރުލުމުގެ ގުޅުން އިތުރަށް ބަދަހިކުރުމަށްޓަކައި އެކުގައި މަސައްކަތް ކުރެވިދާނެކަމުގައި އަޅުގަނޑު ޔަޤީންކުރަމެވެ.

މަނިކުފާނަށް ދުޅަހެޔޮ ސިއްހަތާއި އެސްޓޯނިއާގެ ރައްޔިތުންނަށް އިތުރު ސުލްހަ އާއި ތަނަވަސްކަން ލިބުމަށް އަޅުގަނޑު އެދެމެވެ.

އަޅުގަނޑު މަނިކުފާނަށް ކުރާ މަތިވެރި ޤަދަރު އައުކޮށް، އެކަން ޔަޤީންކަން އެރުވުމަށް، މި ފުރުސަތު ބޭނުންކުރީމެވެ."

ނިމުނީ.

en.title: Minister Dr. Abdulla Khaleel sends Republic Day greetings to the Foreign Minister of Guyana
en.description: The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives, Dr. Abdulla Khaleel sends message of felicitations to the Minister for Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation of the Cooperative Republic of Guyana…
en.body:
Ref: 2025/PR/50

The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives, Dr. Abdulla Khaleel sends message of felicitations to the Minister for Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation of the Cooperative Republic of Guyana, Hugh Hilton Todd on the occasion of the Republic Day of Guyana

Minister’s message reads as follows:

“On behalf of the Government, the people of the Republic of Maldives and on my own behalf, I would like to extend sincere congratulations to Your Excellency, the Government and the people of Guyana, on the occasion of your Republic Day.

The Maldives and Guyana are united in addressing our shared challenges to climate change, our countries exemplify the strength of Small Island Developing States (SIDS). I look forward to working with you to further enhance collaboration in the years ahead.

Please accept, Excellency, the assurances of my highest consideration.”

ENDS

en.title: Minister Dr. Khaleel sends National Day greetings to Brunei
en.description: The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives, His Excellency Dr. Abdulla Khaleel has sent a letter of felicitation to Honourable Dato Erywan Yusof, Minister for Foreign Affairs II of Brunei Darussalam, on…
en.body:
Ref: 2025/PR/49

The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives, His Excellency Dr. Abdulla Khaleel has sent a letter of felicitation to Honourable Dato Erywan Yusof, Minister for Foreign Affairs II of Brunei Darussalam, on the auspicious occasion of their National Day.

In his letter to the Minister of Foreign Affairs II of Brunei Darussalam, Minister Dr. Khaleel extended warm congratulations and greetings to the Minister, the Government and the people of Brunei on the joyous occasion of their National Day.

dv.title: ބްރޫނާއީގެ ޤައުމީ ދުވަހުގެ މުނާސަބަތުގައި އެޤައުމުގެ ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރަށް ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގެ ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރު ތަހުނިޔާ އަރިސްކުރައްވައިފި
dv.description: ބްރޫނާއީގެ ޤައުމީ ދުވަހުގެ މުނާސަބަތުގައި އެޤައުމުގެ ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރު، އޮނަރަބަލް ދާތޯ އެރުވަން ޔޮސޮފް އަށް ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގެ ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރު، ޑޮކްޓަރ ޢަބްދުﷲ ޚަލީލް ތަހުނިޔާ އަރިސްކުރައްވާ ސިޓީފުޅެއް ފޮނުއްވައިފިއެވެ.
dv.body:
‏‎Ref: 2025/PR/49

ބްރޫނާއީގެ ޤައުމީ ދުވަހުގެ މުނާސަބަތުގައި އެޤައުމުގެ ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރު، އޮނަރަބަލް ދާތޯ އެރުވަން ޔޮސޮފް އަށް ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގެ ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރު، ޑޮކްޓަރ ޢަބްދުﷲ ޚަލީލް ތަހުނިޔާ އަރިސްކުރައްވާ ސިޓީފުޅެއް ފޮނުއްވައިފިއެވެ.

‏‎އެމަނިކުފާނުގެ ސިޓީފުޅުގައި، ބްރޫނާއީގެ ޤައުމީ ދުވަހުގެ އުފާވެރި މުނާސަބާގައި، ބުރޫނާއީގެ ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރަށާއި، ބްރޫނާއީގެ ސަރުކާރަށް އަދި އެޤައުމުގެ ރައްޔިތުންނަށް، ދިވެހި ސަރުކާރާއި ދިވެހި ރައްޔިތުންގެ ނަމުގައި، އަދި އެމަނިކުފާނުގެ އަމިއްލަ ނަންފުޅުގައި، ތަހުނިޔާ އާއި ހެޔޮއެދުންތައް އަރިސްކުރައްވާފައިވެއެވެ.

އަދި ދިވެހިރާއްޖެ އާ ބްރޫނާއީ އާ ދެމެދު އޮންނަ ޒަމާންވީ ރަޙްމަތްތެރިކަމުގެ ގުޅުމަކީ އިޙްތިރާމާއި އިތުބާރުގެ މައްޗަށް ބިނާވެފައިވާ އޮންނަ ގާތް ގުޅުމެއްކަމާއި ދެޤައުމުގެ ގުޅުން އިތުރަށް ބަދަހިކޮށް ހަރުދަނާކުރުމަށް އުއްމީދުކުރައްވާ ކަމުގައި ވިދާޅުވެފައިވެއެވެ.

en.title: Minister Dr. Khaleel sends Greetings to the Foreign Minister of Japan on the Occasion of the Birthday of His Imperial Majesty Emperor Naruhito
en.description: Minister of Foreign Affairs Dr. Abdulla Khaleel sent a message of felicitations to the Minister for Foreign Affairs of Japan, Takeshi Iwaya, on the auspicious occasion of the Birthday of His Imperial Majesty Emperor…
en.body:
Ref: 2025/PR/48

Minister of Foreign Affairs Dr. Abdulla Khaleel sent a message of felicitations to the Minister for Foreign Affairs of Japan, Takeshi Iwaya, on the auspicious occasion of the Birthday of His Imperial Majesty Emperor Naruhito.

Minister’s message reads as follows:

“On the auspicious occasion of the Birthday of His Imperial Majesty Emperor Naruhito, I wish to extend warm greetings and sincere good wishes to Your Excellency and the friendly people of Japan.

As Japan celebrated the 70th anniversary of its Official Development Assistance (ODA) last year, Maldives and its people fondly remember Japan's generosity that resonates throughout our archipelago. This enduring friendship, built on mutual respect and shared values, transcends diplomatic boundaries and is fortified by deep-rooted people-to-people ties. Throughout our post-independence journey, Japan has been unmatched in the sheer magnitude of support that it has offered to the Maldives.

I remain confident that under the leadership of His Excellency Dr. Mohamed Muizzu, President of the Republic of Maldives, the enduring bonds of friendship between our two peoples and our countries will continue to strengthen in the years to come.

Please accept, Excellency, my best wishes for your success, good health and well-being and for the peace, progress and prosperity of the people of Japan.”

ENDS

en.title: Foreign Minister Dr. Khaleel sends Independence Day greetings to the Foreign Minister of Saint Lucia.
en.description: The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives, Dr. Abdulla Khaleel sends a message of felicitations to the Minister for External Affairs International Trade, Civil Aviation and Diaspora Affairs, Alva…
en.body:
Ref: 2025/PR/47

The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives, Dr. Abdulla Khaleel sends a message of felicitations to the Minister for External Affairs International Trade, Civil Aviation and Diaspora Affairs, Alva Romanus Baptiste, on the occasion of the Independence Day of Saint Lucia.

Minister’s message reads as follows:

“On behalf of the Government and people of the Republic of Maldives, and on my own behalf, I extend warm felicitations to Your Excellency, the Government, and the people of Saint Lucia, as you celebrate your Independence Day.

As fellow Small Island Developing States (SIDS), I am confident that the bond of friendship between our two nations will grow stronger in the coming years on areas of mutual interest.

Please accept, Excellency, the assurances of my highest consideration”

ENDS.

en.title: Minister of Foreign Affairs, Dr. Abdulla Khaleel concludes his Official Visit to Sri Lanka
en.description: The Minister of Foreign Affairs, Dr. Abdulla Khaleel concluded his Official Visit to Sri Lanka today. The visit undertaken on the invitation of Hon. Vijitha Herath, Minister of Foreign Affairs of Sri Lanka aimed to…
en.body:
Ref: 2025/PR/46

The Minister of Foreign Affairs, Dr. Abdulla Khaleel concluded his Official Visit to Sri Lanka today. The visit undertaken on the invitation of Hon. Vijitha Herath, Minister of Foreign Affairs of Sri Lanka aimed to enhance the longstanding bilateral, economic and cultural ties that exist between both countries.

During the visit, Foreign Minister Dr. Khaleel and Foreign Minister of Sri Lanka, Honourable Vijitha Herath held official talks and discussed enhancing collaboration in key sectors including trade, investment, environment and fisheries.

Foreign Minister Dr. Khaleel also paid courtesy calls on President, Honourable Anura Kumara Disanayake, and Prime Minister, Honourable Dr. Harini Amarasuriya where he congratulated the leadership on the successful presidential and parliamentary elections and the significant progress made in Sri Lanka’s economic recovery.

During the interactions with the business community and investors in Sri Lanka, Foreign Minister Dr. Khaeel shared information on opportunities and insights into investing in the Maldives.

During the visit, Foreign Minister Khaleel met with the Maldivian community residing in Sri Lanka and inquired about their well-being. In addition, Foreign Minister visited the High Commission of the Maldives and the Maldives Centre in Sri Lanka and met with the staff and emphasised the key role played by the mission in supporting the Maldivians residing and travelling to Sri Lanka.

Foreign Minister Dr. Khaleel also met with non-resident Ambassadors and High Commissioners accredited to the Maldives based in Colombo and shared the priorities of the Government of Maldives in its quest to become a developed nation by 2040, and invited them to contribute to the journey.

Foreign Minister Dr. Khaleel was accompanied by Foreign Secretary Fathimath Inaya and Additional Secretary Aminath Abdulla Didi.

ENDS

en.title: Minister Dr. Abdulla Khaleel pays courtesy call on President of Sri Lanka
en.description: Minister of Foreign Affairs, Dr. Abdulla Khaleel paid a courtesy call on the President of the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka, Honourable Anura Kumara Dissanayaka.
en.body:
Ref: 2025/PR/45

Minister of Foreign Affairs, Dr. Abdulla Khaleel paid a courtesy call on the President of the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka, Honourable Anura Kumara Dissanayaka.

During the meeting held at Presidential Secretariat, Minister Dr. Khaleel conveyed greetings and best wishes from President Dr. Muizzu and the people of Maldives.

Minister Dr. Khaleel highlighted the key aspects of the Maldives - Sri Lanka relations and expressed keen interest of the Government of Maldives to explore new avenues to collaborate further to strengthen the close bonds of friendship between the two countries.

On behalf of President Dr. Muizzu and people of Maldives, Minister Khaleel expressed heartfelt appreciation to the Government and people of Sri Lanka for the kind support and assistance rendered to the developmental efforts of Maldives at all times.  
  
Foreign Minister Dr. Khaleel was accompanied by Fathimath Inaya, Foreign Secretary of Maldives, Masood Imad, High Commissioner of Maldives to Sri Lanka, Aminath Abdulla Didi, Additional Secretary at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Maldives.

ENDS

en.title: Minister Dr. Abdulla Khaleel pays a courtesy call on Prime Minister of Sri Lanka
en.description: Minister of Foreign Affairs, Dr. Abdulla Khaleel paid a courtesy call on the Prime Minister of the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka, Honourable Dr. Harini Amarasuriya today.
en.body:
Ref: 2025/PR/44

Minister of Foreign Affairs, Dr. Abdulla Khaleel paid a courtesy call on the Prime Minister of the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka, Honourable Dr. Harini Amarasuriya today.

Minister Dr. Khaleel congratulated Prime Minister for the successful presidential and parliamentary elections and conveyed greetings from President Dr. Muizzu and people of Maldives.

During the meeting, Minister expressed profound gratitude for the Sri Lanka’s unwavering support for the Maldives’ development and progress over the decades especially in the field of education and human resource development and hosting large community of Maldivians in Sri Lanka.

Prime Minister reaffirmed the commitment of the Government of Sri Lanka to work together to strengthen the existing close cooperation between the two countries in multiple areas.

Foreign Minister Dr. Khaleel was accompanied by Foreign Secretary Fathimath Inaya, High Commissioner of Maldives Masood Imad, Additional Secretary at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs Aminath Abdulla Didi, Deputy High Commissioner Fathimath Ghina, and Second Secretary Aminath Warudha.

ENDS

en.title: Minister Khaleel sends greetings on the occasion of the 50th anniversary of diplomatic ties between the Maldives and Singapore
en.description: The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives, His Excellency Dr. Abdulla Khaleel has sent a letter of felicitation to His Excellency Dr. Vivian Balakrishnan, Minister for Foreign Affairs of the Republic…
en.body:
Ref: 2025/PR/43

The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives, His Excellency Dr. Abdulla Khaleel has sent a letter of felicitation to His Excellency Dr. Vivian Balakrishnan, Minister for Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Singapore, in connection with the 50th anniversary of diplomatic relations between the Republic of Maldives and the Republic of Singapore.

On the auspicious occasion of 50 years of strong diplomatic ties and friendly relations between the two countries, Minister Dr. Khaleel extend warm greetings and conveyed that the historic milestone stands as a testament to the enduring partnership between the two countries.

Minister Dr. Khaleel noted the close friendship between Maldives and Singapore that has flourished over the years through people-to-people exchanges, educational collaborations, and trade and economic ties and thanked the Government and the people of Singapore for their continued assistance and cooperation to the Maldives over the years.

He also reiterated his commitment to working closely with Singapore both bilaterally and in the multilateral fora and extended warm wishes to Minister Dr. Balakrishnan and the people of Singapore.

ENDS

dv.title: ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއާއި ސިންގަޕޫރާ ދެމެދު ޤާއިމުކޮށްފައިވާ ސިޔާސީ ގުޅުމަށް 50 އަހަރު ފުރުމުގެ މުނާސަބަތުގައި އެޤައުމުގެ ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރު، ޑޮކްޓަރ ވިވިއަން ބާލަކްރިޝްނަން އަށް ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގެ ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރު ޑޮކްޓަރ ޢަބްދުﷲ ޚަލީލް ތަހުނިޔާ ފޮނުއްވައިފި
dv.description: ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއާއި ސިންގަޕޫރާ ދެމެދު ޤާއިމުކޮށްފައިވާ ސިޔާސީ ގުޅުމަށް 50 އަހަރު ފުރުމުގެ މުނާސަބަތުގައި އެޤައުމުގެ ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރު، ޑޮކްޓަރ ވިވިއަން ބާލަކްރިޝްނަން އަށް ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގެ ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރު، ޑޮކްޓަރ ޢަބްދުﷲ ޚަލީލް…

Ref: 2025/PR/43

ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއާއި ސިންގަޕޫރާ ދެމެދު ޤާއިމުކޮށްފައިވާ ސިޔާސީ ގުޅުމަށް 50 އަހަރު ފުރުމުގެ މުނާސަބަތުގައި އެޤައުމުގެ ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރު، ޑޮކްޓަރ ވިވިއަން ބާލަކްރިޝްނަން އަށް ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގެ ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރު، ޑޮކްޓަރ ޢަބްދުﷲ ޚަލީލް ތަހުނިޔާގެ ސިޓީފުޅެއް ފޮނުއްވައިފިއެވެ.  
ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރުގެ ސިޓީފުޅުގައި، ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއާއި ސިންގަޕޫރާއި ދެމެދު ޤާއިމުކޮށްފައިވާ ސިޔާސީ އަދި ރަހުމަތްތެރިކަމުގެ ގާތް ގުޅުމަށް 50 އަހަރު ފުރުމުގެ އުފާވެރި މުނާސަބަތުގެ ތަހުނިޔާ އާއި ހެޔޮއެދުންތައް ފޮނުވުމާއިއެކު، މިއީ ދެޤައުމުގެ ގުޅުމުގެ ތެރެއިން ފާހަގަކޮށްލެވޭ ތާރީޚީ މޭލުގާއެއްކަންވެސް އެމަނިކުފާނު ފާހަގަ ކުރެއްވިއެވެ.

އަދި ދެޤައުމުގެ ރަޚްމަތްތެރިކަމުގެ ގުޅުން ވޭތުވިއަހަރުތަކުގައި ބަދަހިވެގެންގޮސްފައިވަނީ، ރައްޔިތުންގެ މެދުގައި އޮންނަ ގުޅުމުގެ ތެރެއިންނާއި، ތަޢުލީމާއި، ވިޔަފާރިާއި އަދި އިޤްތިޞާދީ ގުޅުންތަކުގެ ތެރެއިންކަންވެސް ފާހަގަ ކުރެއްވިއެވެ. މީގެ އިތުރުން، ސިންގަޕޫރު ސަރުކާރާއި ރައްޔިތުން ރާއްޖެއަށް އެކިދާއިރާތަކުން ވެދެއްވަމުން ގެންދަވާ އެހީތެރިކަމާއި އެއްބާރުލެއްވުމަށް އެމަނިކުފާނު ޝުކުރު އަދާކުރެއްވިއެވެ.

މީގެއިތުރުން، ދެޤައުމުގެ ދެމެދުގައި އޮތް ގާތް ގުޅުން އިތުރަށް ހަރުދަނާކޮށް ބައިނަލްއަޤްވާމީ މަސްރަހްގައި ސިންގަޕޫރާިއެކު ގާތުން މަސައްކަތްކުރާނޭ ކަމުގެ ޔަޤީންކަންްވެސް އެމަނިކުފާނު ސިންގަޕޫރުގެ ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރަށް ދެއްވިއެވެ.  
ނިމުނީ
